slides.title: Women's dress and silver
slides.text: Saudi women's dress and jewelry are the richest part of the heritage, and the hardest to bring into a quiet brand. Today you learn what they meant, then practice the key skill of A'ila Areeqa: turning a feminine detail into a masculine one, without losing where it came from.

slides.q: What were the small triangle openings in Najdi walls for?
options: Air, light and a view out, and also defense
slides.why: Air, light and a view out, and defense. A useful hole that became a pattern.
whys: They look decorative, but each one had a job.
Rain is rare in Najd, and these sit high on the wall.
They're openings, not shelves.

hint.cap: Small openings, high on a thick wall, in a hot desert.

slides.q: Best lining for a jacket worn in Gulf heat?
slides.why: Cupro breathes best. Half-line it, and keep the sleeves lined.
whys: Polyester breathes poorly: the cheap-suit lining.
Acetate is light but weak.
Rubber doesn't breathe at all.

slides.q: In the pinch test, a loose third layer floating inside the jacket front means…
slides.why: Canvas. It's sewn, not glued, so it floats as its own layer.
whys: Fused is the opposite: glued flat, no loose layer.
The pinch test checks the front's inside, not the lining.
The pinch test isn't about lining fabric.

hint.cap: Outside, a layer, lining. Which layer floats?

slides.caption: Drawing of a Najdi overdress: wide T-shape, very wide sleeves, embroidered neck.
slides.title: Najd: the mesh-strainer dress
text: Najdi women's dress was loose and long, to the ankle or floor, with embroidery. Early colors were muted grey and navy. Brighter colors came later. Many women cut and sewed their own clothes.
For special occasions they wore the thawb najdi: a huge T-shaped overdress of sheer tulle with very wide sleeves, embroidered at the neck front and back.
Locally it is called munaykhal, "mesh strainer", because the cloth is full of tiny holes.
slides.note: No free-to-use photo of a Saudi women's traditional dress exists online that we can show here. The drawing is based on the Zay Initiative's museum notes. Search "thawb najdi Zay Initiative" to see real ones.
src: Arab News: the revival of Najdi fashion
Saudipedia: Women's garments in the First Saudi State

slides.title: Three regions, three looks
slides.intro: There was never one Saudi women's wardrobe. Climate, trade and materials made each region different.
layers: Loose and long. Sheer overdresses over a base dress. Started with muted grey and navy.
Shaped by trade and pilgrimage. Ceremonial dress is white with gold zari thread.
Many-colored robes with geometric patterns and flower headpieces. Asiri women wore straw hats to work in the sun.
slides.note: Notice the pattern: the south is bright, the center is muted, the west is white and gold. For a quiet brand, Najd's muted palette is the closest fit.
src: Arab News: the revival of Najdi fashion

slides.caption: Amber and silver, Yemen. Southern Arabian jewelry shared this style.
slides.title: Silver was a woman's bank
text: Part of a bride's dowry bought her jewelry. It belonged to her alone. In hard times she could sell it. It was her safety net.
Southern pieces were mostly big silver with few stones, decorated with fine silver wire. They used amber, fire agate, blood coral and old glass beads. Ra'af means deep red coral beads.
In Najran: kharous (earrings), harouz (necklaces), halqah (head piece), lazem and shamiliyyat (wide bracelets), marda' (rings). Some bracelets weighed about 200 grams.

slides.caption: An Omani hirz necklace: a hollow pendant that held Qur'an verses or herbs.
slides.title: Heard, but not seen
text: Some necklace cases held verses of the Qur'an. Turquoise was worn against the evil eye.
Tiny bells hung from many pieces. As a woman walked, the bells told people she was near, so men looked away. She was heard, but not seen.
Bedouin silver also used carnelian, turquoise, bells and coins. In Saudi Arabia, silversmiths worked in Riyadh's Batha souq and in Taif.
slides.note: The bell is a sound that says "I'm here" without being seen. That's a perfect quiet-luxury idea.

slides.title: Two necklaces, two ideas

left.label: Coins and chains
left.caption: Silver necklace from Yemen, 1800s to early 1900s. Fowler Museum, Los Angeles.

slides.takeaway: Left: weight and sound, from many dangling pieces. Right: fine wire worked into lace. For a men's piece, keep one idea only: either one small dangling bead, or a little filigree texture on a button. Never both.

slides.caption: Silkworms spinning cocoons on a frame, Da Lat, Vietnam.
slides.title: Where silk comes from
text: Silk is spun by silkworms. Each worm wraps itself in one long thread to make a cocoon.
Cocoons are boiled to loosen the thread, then it is unwound. That's why silk is so smooth: it's one long filament, not short fibers twisted together.
Silk breathes and feels cool, but it's delicate and shows water and sweat marks easily.

slides.title: From cocoon to cloth

left.label: Boiling cocoons
left.caption: Traditional Thai silk making: cocoons in hot water.

right.label: Charmeuse
right.caption: Silk charmeuse: shiny face, dull back.

slides.takeaway: Charmeuse is woven in a satin weave, which is why it shines. You met satin in Lesson 2: long floating threads, smooth and shiny, but it shows every mark.

slides.title: Silk weight: momme
slides.intro: Silk is weighed in momme. Higher number = heavier, thicker cloth. One momme is about 4.3 grams per square meter.
slides.note: One silk maker says light, open, matte silks of about 7–14 momme let heat out best, and shiny silks show sweat. That's one company's advice, not lab data, so test before you buy.

slides.title: Which silk for the Gulf?
slides.intro: Same fiber, different weaves. Each feels different in the heat.
layers: Plain weave, soft sheen, light. Clings little. Good in heat.
Twisted yarn, matte, pebbly. Matte may hide sweat better.
Sheer and crinkly. Good for loose layers, like the Najdi overdress.
Glossy face, dull back. Clings and shows sweat.
slides.note: Rule for A'ila Areeqa: for hot-weather abayas and linings, choose light, matte, plain or crepe silks under about 16 momme. Keep glossy charmeuse for evening pieces or small accents.
src: Anuprerna: is silk good for hot weather

slides.title: Move 13: The silent bell
slides.text: A woman's bell said "I'm here" without being seen. Turn it into a men's detail that says the same thing, quietly.
how: One small closed silver bead on a drawstring end or a zip pull.
No clapper inside, so it's silent. Only the wearer knows what it was.
Inside a cuff: one stitch in deep coral red, a nod to ra'af beads.

slides.title: Move 14: The munaykhal layer
slides.text: The Najdi overdress was a sheer "mesh strainer" layer over a solid dress. Keep the layering idea, change the shape.
how: Men: a dark open-weave summer overshirt over a white thobe or tee.
Sharper shoulders, straight cut, no embroidery.
Women: georgette in Najd's muted grey or navy, long and wide-sleeved.

slides.title: Move 15: The muted palette
slides.text: Najdi women started with grey and navy before brighter colors arrived. That's already a quiet-luxury palette.
how: Base colors: Najdi grey, navy, sand.
One accent only: coral red (ra'af) or zari gold, used small.
Use it for both men and women, so the brand looks like one family.

slides.title: Feminine to masculine
slides.text: Pick one women's piece from this lesson and turn it into a men's detail.
checklist: Name the women's piece (dress, bell, necklace or bracelet)
Say what you keep: the idea, the material or the shape
Say what you drop, and where your men's detail goes on the garment

context: Najran jewelry includes kharous (earrings), harouz (necklaces), halqah (head piece), lazem and shamiliyyat (wide bracelets) and marda' (rings).

Southern jewelry was mostly big silver with few stones, decorated with silver wire and plates. It used fire agate, amber, blood coral (ra'af = deep red coral beads) and old glass beads. Bedouin silver also used carnelian, turquoise, bells and coins.
Jewelry was bought with part of the bride price and was the woman's own property and safety net, sold in hard times. Some necklace cases held Qur'an verses; turquoise was worn against the evil eye.
Tiny bells let people know a woman was near, so men looked away: 'heard but not seen'.
Move 13 idea: for men, one small closed silver bead or a bell with no clapper (silent) on a drawstring end or zip pull, or one coral-red stitch inside a cuff.
Najdi women's dress: loose shapes, ankle or floor length, with embroidery. Early colors were muted grey and navy; brighter colors came later. Many women sewed and cut their own clothes.

The Najdi overdress (thawb najdi) is a huge T-shape of sheer tulle with very wide sleeves and big underarm panels, embroidered at the neck front and back. Locally called munaykhal, 'mesh strainer', because the cloth is full of holes. Worn for special occasions.
Hijaz ceremonial dress is white with gold zari thread; Asir and Jazan dress is many-colored with geometric patterns and floral headpieces.
Move 14 idea (feminine to masculine): keep the idea of a sheer open layer over a solid one; for men, a dark open-weave summer overshirt over a white thobe or tee, sharper shoulders, no embroidery.

checklist: Choose a silk type and momme for the lining
Choose one for the evening scarf
slides.notePrompt: Lining: ___ at ___ momme because... Scarf: ___ because...
context: Momme is silk's weight: higher number = heavier cloth. One momme is about 4.3 grams per square meter, so 16 momme is about 69 grams per square meter.

Habotai: plain, soft sheen, 8–16 momme, low cling, good in heat. Crepe de chine: twisted yarn, matte, pebbly, 12–16 momme. Georgette: sheer, crinkly, 5–10 momme. Charmeuse: glossy face, dull back, 12–30 momme, clings and shows sweat.
One silk maker says shiny silks show sweat and heavy dense weaves trap heat; open plain weaves of about 7–14 momme let heat out best. This is one company's advice, not lab data.
Rule for A'ila Areeqa: for hot-weather abayas and linings, light matte plain or crepe silks under about 16 momme; keep glossy charmeuse for evening or small accents.

slides.q: Why did a bride's silver matter so much?
options: It was her own property and safety net
It was rented for the wedding
slides.why: It belonged to her alone, and she could sell it in hard times.
whys: It was beautiful, but its real job was security.
It was bought with part of the dowry, and it was hers.
It was hers to keep.

slides.q: What did the tiny bells on jewelry do?
options: Let people know a woman was near, so men looked away
slides.why: "Heard, but not seen." The sound gave her privacy.
whys: Nice idea, but the sources tie the bells to people, not animals.
That was not their stated purpose.
The bells were worn every day, not just for dances.

slides.q: Why was the Najdi overdress called munaykhal, "mesh strainer"?
options: It was used in the kitchen
Its sheer cloth is full of tiny holes
slides.why: The sheer tulle is full of tiny holes, like a strainer.
whys: It's a dress, not a kitchen tool. The name describes the cloth.
It's sheer tulle, not metal.
It was a special-occasion dress for women.

hint.cap: Look closely at the outer layer.

slides.q: What does a higher momme number tell you about silk?
slides.why: Momme is weight. Higher = heavier, thicker cloth.
whys: Shine comes from the weave, like satin, not the momme.
Momme has nothing to do with age.
Heavier silk usually costs more, not less.

slides.q: Best silk for a summer abaya lining?
options: Light matte habotai or crepe de chine
slides.why: Light, matte, plain or crepe silk under about 16 momme.
whys: Charmeuse clings and shows sweat. Keep it for evening.
That's not silk, and polyester traps heat.
Twill is heavier and medium in heat.

slides.q: Turning a woman's bell into a men's detail, what do you keep?
options: The idea: a small silver piece that marks presence quietly
slides.why: Keep the idea and the material. Drop the sound and the size.
whys: The point of Move 13 is a silent bell.
Copying the necklace shape keeps it feminine.
One small piece, not many.

slides.title: Three things to keep
items: Silver was a woman's bank; bells meant "heard, not seen".
Move 13: one silent silver bead, one coral-red stitch.
Munaykhal = a sheer "mesh strainer" layer over a solid one.
Move 14: open-weave overshirt for men. Najd's grey and navy for both.
Momme = silk weight. Light, matte silk for heat.
Habotai or crepe under about 16 momme. Charmeuse for evening only.
